# Installation & Setup

## Overview

The course materials are designed to be run on a personal computer.
All of the software and data used are freely available online, and instructions on how to obtain them are provided below.


## Step 1: Install Python

In this course, we will be using Python 3 with some of its most popular scientific libraries.

Python 3 itself can be downloaded and installed from <https://www.python.org/downloads/>.
Follow the steps on this website to download and install *Python 3.14.x* for Windows or MacOS. Just ask for help during the practical sessions or on Teams when something isn't clear. 


## Step 2: Install Jupyter Lab

We will teach the basics of Python programming using the [Jupyter Lab](https://jupyter.org/), a scripting environment that runs 
in a web browser.

Follow these steps to install Jupyter Lab:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Windows
1. Open a Windows [PowerShell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerShell) terminal.

2. Create a directory for the course, for example `pmi`, and enter it:
   ```powershell
   cd ~       # Changes directory to your home directory.
   mkdir pmi  # Makes a directory named 'pmi'.
   cd pmi     # Changes directory into 'pmi'. 
   ```

3. Inside the `pmi` directory, run this command to create a so-called *virtual environment* (venv):
   ```powershell
   py -V:3.14 -m venv .venv  # Creates a Python 3.14 virtual environment in '.venv'
   ```

4. Activate the virtual environment:
   ```powershell
   .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1  # Runs the script 'Activate.ps1' to activate the virtual environment.
   ```
   The terminal should now show the name of the virtual environment in front of the prompt.

5. Install the *packages* `jupyterlab`, `numpy`, `matplotlib`, `pandas`, `pillow` and `pydicom` in the virtual environment.
   These are packages that we will use throughout the course. 
   ```powershell
   pip install jupyterlab numpy matplotlib ipympl pandas pillow pydicom pylibjpeg pylibjpeg-libjpeg pyside6  # Installs several packages.
   ```
   *(Note: this may take a few minutes.)*

6. Start Jupyter Lab:
   ```powershell
   jupyter-lab  # Starts Jupyter Lab.
   ```

7. When you're finished with Jupyter Lab, just close the Windows terminal and browser tab.

When you need to start Jupyter Lab again, just repeat steps 4 and 6.

## MacOS 
1. Open the [Terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminal_(macOS)) app.

2. Create a directory for the course, for example `pmi`, and enter it:
   ```zsh
   cd ~       # Changes directory to your home directory.
   mkdir pmi  # Makes a directory named 'pmi'.
   cd pmi     # Changes directory into 'pmi'. 
   ```

3. Inside the `pmi` directory, run this command to create a so-called *virtual environment*:
   ```zsh
   python3.14 -m venv .venv  # Creates a Python 3.14 virtual environment in '.venv'
   ```

4. Activate the virtual environment:
   ```zsh
   source .venv/bin/activate  # Runs the script 'activate' to activate the virtual environment.
   ```
   The terminal should now show the name of the virtual environment in front of the prompt.

5. Install the *packages* `jupyterlab`, `numpy`, `matplotlib`, `pandas`, `pillow` and `pydicom` in the virtual environment.
   These are packages that we will use throughout the course.
   ```zsh
   pip install jupyterlab numpy matplotlib ipympl pandas pillow pydicom pylibjpeg pylibjpeg-libjpeg pyside6  # Installs several packages.
   ```
   *(Note: this may take a few minutes.)*

6. Start Jupyter Lab:
   ```zsh
   jupyter-lab  # Starts Jupyter Lab.
   ```

7. When you're finished with Jupyter Lab, just close the terminal app and browser tab.

When you need to start Jupyter Lab again, just repeat steps 4 and 6.

## FAQ
> *I'm getting the error `Program 'pip.exe' failed to run: This program is blocked by group policy.`*

Try running `python -m pip` instead.

> *I'm getting the error `Program 'jupyter-lab.exe' failed to run: This program is blocked by group policy.`*

Try running `python -m jupyterlab` instead.

> Executing `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1` just opens the file in Notepad.

This script is meant to be executed in a Windows [PowerShell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerShell) terminal.
From a classic Windows Command Prompt, you could run `.\.venv\Scripts\Activate.bat` instead.

:::

## Course Materials {#course-materials}

Now you've installed Python and Jupyter Lab, you're ready to download and open the course materials.

### Step 1: Obtain course materials

1. Download the zip file with all [course materials](https://github.com/umcu-isi/programming-for-medical-imaging/releases/download/course-materials/course_materials.zip).
2. Unzip the zip file in your `pmi` directory.

In your `pmi` directory, you will now see a folder called `images` and several `.ipynb` files. The directory structure should now look like:

```
pmi/
├── .venv/
│   └── ...
├── images/
│   ├── ct_jaw/
│   ├── ct_jaw.nii.gz
│   └── ...
├── scripting.ipynb
├── functions.ipynb
└── ...
```

### Step 2: Open the assignments

Follow these steps to start JupyterLab and open the assignments for the relevant week:

::: {.panel-tabset}
## Windows
1. Open a Windows [PowerShell](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/PowerShell) terminal and change to your `pmi` directory.

2. Activate the virtual environment:
   ```powershell
   .\.venv\Scripts\Activate.ps1
   ```
   The terminal should now show the name of the virtual environment in front of the prompt.

3. Start Jupyter Lab:
   ```powershell
   jupyter-lab
   ```
   
4. Once the browser window opens, double-click the `.ipynb` notebook file for the relevant week in the file browser on the left.

When you need to start Jupyter Lab again, just repeat steps 4 and 6.

## MacOS 
1. Open the [Terminal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Terminal_(macOS)) app and change to your `pmi` directory.

2. Activate the virtual environment:
   ```zsh
   source .venv/bin/activate
   ```
   The terminal should now show the name of the virtual environment in front of the prompt.

3. Start Jupyter Lab:
   ```zsh
   jupyter-lab
   ```
   
4. Once the browser window opens, double-click the `.ipynb` notebook file for the relevant week in the file browser on the left.

:::
